# <span id="aanchor364"></span> About Locations

A location is a collection of one or more meters and/or other locations. Locations are used for balancing, determining pipeline efficiency and reporting (such as producer total volumes, fuel by area, or emissions reporting). Within a location, member data is totaled or averaged, and is available at an hourly, daily, or monthly basis.

In the following example, five meter members have been added to a location. When the location is rolled up, the volume and energy values are totaled, and the values for pressure and heating are averaged using weighted averaging.

|       | Volume | Energy | Pressure | Heat Value |
|:-----:|:------:|:------:|:--------:|:----------:|
| MET_1 | 100.0  | 105.0  |  150.0   |   1050.0   |
| MET_2 | 100.0  | 105.0  |  175.0   |   1050.0   |
| MET_3 | 100.0  | 105.0  |  125.0   |   1050.0   |
| MET_4 | 200.0  | 220.0  |  165.0   |   1100.0   |
| MET_5 | 200.0  | 220.0  |  145.0   |   1100.0   |
| LOC1  | 700.0  | 755.0  |  152.9   |   1078.6   |

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Segment">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Segment</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Segment">

A segment is a physical or logical section of a pipeline; made up of meters and/or other locations.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 168;height: 33;" />

#### Data Considerations

All segments require a base direction. The segment’s direction represents its general contribution to the overall system and dictate how the total is calculated:

- **Inlet**: Total = \[(Sum of Inlets) – (Sum of Outlets)\]
- **Outlet**: Total = \[(Sum of Outlets) – (Sum of Inlets)\]

Segment locations with a "Throughput" direction can only have throughput meters as members. Each meter member will designated as having a positive or negative contribution to the location. Those specifications are used in calculating the total:

- **Throughput:** Total = \[(Sum of Positives) – (Sum of Negatives)\]

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Station">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Station</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Station">

Station locations are used to total all meter runs associated with a meter station, such as multiple tubes delivering to a power plant, multiple wellheads at a pad location, or large volume interconnects between pipelines.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 69;height: 58;" />

#### Data Considerations

The station location can be classified as an inlet or outlet; however, member meters are all additive to the station location. The following rules are true of stations:

- A station can contain only meter members, therefore neither a segment nor another station can be a member of a station.
- A meter cannot belong to two stations at the same time.
- A station is a physical location.
- Meter members are all additive to the station location whether they are classified as an inlet or outlet.

 

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Balance">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Balance</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Balance">

A balance is a segment with properties for balancing a pipeline system; consists of a closed system of inlets and outlets; can contain any type of member (meters, stations, segments, and other balances).

<br/>![](data:image/png;base64,)

#### Data Considerations

The expectation of a balance system is that everything is accounted for and the total product received into the system will equal the total product delivered out of the system. No direction is needed since results are expected to equal zero. However, these totals never completely reach zero; this difference is termed "gain" or "loss."

The default calculation in FLOWCAL is: (Outlets - Inlets)/Inlets

The sign of the result depends on how the balance arithmetic is set up within the Rollup Configuration screen. You can define the numerator and denominator according to operational needs and preferences.

The balance location total will result in a loss if there are more inlets than outlets, or a gain if there are more outlets than inlets.

To successfully balance a system of piping, all inlets and outlets need to be represented. This includes not only conventional meters, tanks, batches, and line pack, but also accounts for items such as fuel used, flared volumes, shrinkage due to treating or processing, and third-party volumes.

Balances at the top of the hierarchy will typically have the "Root Location" option set.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Inventory">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Inventory</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Inventory">

An inventory refers to a segment with properties for inventory tracking. This location aggregates total inventory and calculates changes in inventory. It consists of inventory objects such as line pack meters and other inventory locations, and can be added to balance locations.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 143;height: 126;" />

</div>
